name: Coincheck
rootCause: Unidentified assailants stole 523 million NEM coins (about $534 million) from the exchange's hot wallet. According to Coincheck, NEM coins are kept on a single-signature hot wallet instead of a more secure multi-signature wallet, and the stolen coins are confirmed to be Coincheck customers.

descriptions.text: Unidentified assailants stole 523 million NEM coins (about $534 million) from the exchange's hot wallet. According to Coincheck, NEM coins are kept on a single-signature hot wallet instead of a more secure multi-signature wallet, and the stolen coins are confirmed to be Coincheck customers.

On 26 January 2018, Coincheck's NEM (XEM) hot wallet was compromised, leading to the theft of approximately 523 million XEM (then worth ~$530 million). The attacker gained access through malware installed via a targeted phishing campaign against engineering staff, exploiting the absence of multisig and cold storage. The stolen funds were laundered quickly, resulting in minimal on-chain recovery. Coincheck reimbursed customers from corporate funds and was later acquired by Monex Group. Coincheck is a Japanese exchange that works with multiple blockchains, including NEM. Around January 26, 2018, XEM valued at approximately $400m USD were stolen. Initial cause was unclear to Coincheck according to their statements. After hours of speculation Friday night, Coincheck Inc. said the coins were sent “illicitly” outside the venue. Co-founder Yusuke Otsuka said the company didn’t know how the 500 million tokens went missing, and the firm is working to ensure the safety of all client assets.
